candidates.doc:
executeExileFromGraveyardEffect implements the exile_from_graveyard
primitive (ticket engine.auto-exile-from-graveyard-f671ca6575, Kroxa and
Kunoros class): "you may exile five cards from your graveyard" as a
standalone zone-move effect, distinct from executeExileEffect
(battlefield-target removal, Rule-608.2b fizzle semantics don't apply
here) and the unrelated exileFromGraveyard(card, playerIdx) helper in
activated_abilities.go, which pays a cost by exiling one NAMED card.
effectValue["whose"] selects the referenced player — "you" (default, the
ability's controller) or "opponent" (first other player) — mirroring the
"whose" convention exile_all_from_library above uses; effectValue["amount"]
is the (already dynamic-amount-resolved) card count. Auto-selects from the
front of the graveyard, the same auto-select convention
executeSearchLibraryXAmountToHand (effects.go) uses for its own X-based
zone move, since the engine has no interactive per-card selection UI.
Exiling fewer than amount (an undersized graveyard) is not an error —
Rule 608.2b's "as much as possible" idiom. Returns the actual number of
cards exiled so a linked "when you do" trigger can read it. No resolvable
player or amount <= 0: no-op, 0 exiled.

candidates.description: ManifestCardOntoBattlefield puts card face down onto the battlefield as a
candidates.doc:
ManifestCardOntoBattlefield puts card face down onto the battlefield as a
2/2 creature under playerIdx's control, the same face-down representation
Morph uses (MorphData) but reached from a zone move (library -> battlefield)
rather than a cast from hand. Unlike CastMorph's fixed {3} cast cost, a
manifested permanent's turn-face-up cost is its own printed mana cost
(Rule 701.40a) — and per Rule 701.40b, turning face up is only ever legal
at all if the manifested card is a creature card (see the OriginalType
guard added to TurnFaceUp above); manifested noncreature cards remain face
down for the rest of the game (short of a card-specific effect).

candidates.description: // EntryFromZoneIsVetoed reports whether any permanent on the battlefield
candidates.doc:
EntryFromZoneIsVetoed reports whether any permanent on the battlefield
vetoes card entering the battlefield from fromZone. Land cards are never
vetoed; only graveyard/library origins are watched — entries from other
zones (hand, exile, the stack) are unaffected regardless of who controls
the veto. Consulted by primitives that move a card onto the battlefield
BEFORE removing it from its source zone, so a vetoed card simply stays
where it was.

candidates.doc:
exile-top-of-library-playable vocabulary ([VOCAB] #1068).

The library-top primitives that existed before this either look without
moving (LookAtTopN/RevealTop, see lib_look_reveal_top.go) or move to the
graveyard with no return value (MillPlayer, see lib_mill_single_player.go).
Neither can produce a *game.Card reference to a card that used to be the
top of the library. Meanwhile the play_card_from_exile family
(GrantExilePlay, see lib_exile_play_grant.go) only grants permission on a
card that is ALREADY sitting in exile — it cannot pull one out of the
library itself. Faking "exile the top card of your library, you may play
it" with a library search would let the player choose any card instead of
the forced top card, which is the silently-wrong bug this primitive
exists to avoid.

ExileTopOfLibrary exiles the actual top card of playerIdx's library — the
forced card, never a search or choice — and returns a reference to that
specific card so the caller can act on it further, e.g. hand it straight
to GrantExilePlay to implement "exile the top card of your library; you
may play it this turn" (impulse-draw style effects).
candidates.name: ExileTopOfLibrary
candidates.title: ExileTopOfLibrary

candidates.description: DrawCardWithEvent draws a card for a player and fires the draw event.
candidates.doc:
DrawCardWithEvent draws a card for a player and fires the draw event.

Rule 616/614.16-ish ([VOCAB] #1291): before drawing, checks for an active
draw-replacement effect (e.g. "if you would draw a card, you may instead
search your library for a card, put it into your hand, then shuffle" —
installed via cardfns.GrantDrawReplacement/ReplaceDrawWithLibrarySearch).
If one applies, its substituted action runs INSTEAD of the draw: the card
is never drawn from the library the normal way, and no draw event/trigger
fires below, since a draw never actually happened. This is distinct from a
triggered "whenever you draw a card" reaction, which exists alongside the
real draw rather than replacing it.
